grade.basis: Independently inspected all three pages of the complete Mandozzi score. Cello 1 carries the treble-clef cantus with ornamented thirty-second-note and triplet figures, requiring secure upper-register placement, controlled slurs and expressive sustained bowing. Cellos 2 and 3 also have persistent upper-register, chromatically inflected moving lines; Cello 4 is substantially simpler. The marked very slow quaver = 40 limits velocity demands. Advanced individual cello technique, without a quartet-size uplift; adjacent level 4 remains plausible depending on execution standard.

findings.finding: Complete three-page score identifies BWV 639, arranged for four cellos by Orfeo Mandozzi in 2014. All 18 bars through the final fermata were inspected; the very slow marking and ornamented upper voice are visible in the notation.

grade.basis: Independently inspected the complete three-page, 32-bar arrangement of Variation 22 only. Cello 1 moves between bass and treble clefs and sustains an exposed upper-register line, with shifts and occasional eighth-note movement; Cello 2 also lies high in bass clef. Rhythms are principally halves and quarters with short eighth-note motifs, and there is no passagework or double-stopping requiring diploma technique. Early advanced is an appropriate individual-part estimate, with level 5 plausible for polished upper-register tone and intonation.

findings.finding: Score headed Goldberg Variation 22, Alla Breve, J. S. Bach, arr. Suzanne Dicker. Four cello staves; both repeated halves and the final bar on page 3 inspected. This estimate covers this complete variation, not the Goldberg set.

grade.basis: Independently inspected the public perusal images: introductory note plus every notation page from opening to the final silence (printed score pages 1–10). The first cello opens alone in bass clef and later restates its line in treble clef above the chorale, requiring secure register changes, exposed sustained intonation and long-bow dynamic control. Other upper parts also sustain treble-clef lines; the sixth cello has occasional stopped dyads and arco/pizzicato changes. Rhythmic surface is overwhelmingly long notes with occasional duplet divisions, and the tempo remains unchanged. Level 5 reflects individual upper-register tone and control, not the eight-player ensemble size; level 4 is the adjacent plausible alternative.

findings.finding: Public watermarked perusal supplies the complete visible arc through the closing a niente and final rests. Composer note describes an introduction for first cello, two statements of the chorale, austere homophony and unchanging tempo; duration approximately 4 minutes 30 seconds. Opening marking Con pietà, minim approximately 108, uses very long written note values. The note mentions the 1994 Vale of Glamorgan Festival and copyright is 1994, despite a conflicting 1984 heading in the typed note.
